verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's own API access token docs say tokens can be scoped to restrict the operations they can perform, such as a read-only integration. That is a first-party least-privilege credential mechanism an agent can use. missing for 10: documented depth of scoping (per-project/environment/resource limits, custom roles on tokens), token expiry/rotation details, agent- or MCP-specific guidance on using scoped tokens, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
